rows.user: Actually, let's drop Tauri and move the desktop shell to Electron; the Linux webview bugs are too much.
Scrap Fly.io. Relay gets deployed to our own Kubernetes cluster from now on.
Change of direction on hosting: game servers leave Agones and run on GameLift fleets.
Switch transactional email from Postmark to Amazon SES; SES is far cheaper at our volume.
Instead of Prometheus and Grafana, ship all Relay metrics to Datadog.
Let's make dark the default theme; light becomes the opt-in.
Webhook intake runs through Broadway consuming from SQS these days.
Profiles sit in Aurora Postgres since last week's migration.
Our PDFs come out of a headless Chromium service nowadays.
Search is handled in the front end by a Web Worker running MiniSearch.
Leaderboards update live on every match result, written straight into Redis.
FX rates get pulled every hour from Open Exchange Rates.
The job queue should live in Redis rather than in the database.
Notes will be kept in one SQLite file instead of loose files on disk.
The matchmaker gets rewritten in Go.
Money columns become Decimal fields with four places.
Stored request bodies are retained for 30 days now.
Keep Elixir, but host Relay on Render instead of Fly.
Anti-cheat stays on the server, except aim-assist checks, which move to the client for latency.
Sync still uses the user's own cloud storage, but iCloud Drive replaces Dropbox.
Monterey support is dropped; macOS 13 Ventura is the new minimum.
I've changed my mind about function-head matching; prefer explicit case blocks for readability.
Python line length goes to 88, the black default.
The match results write budget is relaxed to one second.
Send crash reports to Sentry's hosted service instead of our GlitchTip box.
Invoice numbers may restart each fiscal year, as long as they stay sequential within the year.
Replace Serilog with Microsoft.Extensions.Logging and its OpenTelemetry exporter.
Tauri stays; pin it to 2.1 and turn on the updater plugin.
Oban queues are split per plan tier: free, pro and enterprise each get their own queue.
The DynamoDB profile table gets a global secondary index on display name for friend search.
WeasyPrint invoices should embed the company logo at 300 dpi.
Markdown notes keep YAML front matter for tags and dates.
Schema validation failures return a 422 with the failing JSON pointer in the body.
The UDP reliability layer adds forward error correction for voice packets.
Postmark bounces are recorded on the customer record and shown in the UI.
On top of the cold-start budget, a warm start must finish in under 300 ms.
Tenant isolation also needs row-level security policies in Postgres.
Serilog events should also carry the match id.
Integer cents apply to tax amounts as well, not just totals.
Svelte components use TypeScript with strict mode on.
Every deploy from main also runs a smoke test against staging first.
When cross-region matchmaking happens after the EU launch, pick regions by measured player latency.
The S3 bucket for company files lives in eu-central-1.
